safety: READ_ONLY_CATALOG_INITIAL_PRIVILEGES_AND_EFFECTIVE_PERMISSION_METADATA; no private user rows or secret values
scope: Complete ordered pg_init_privs first-install privilege records 1-233; explicit current privilege sample separately; not native compiled or hosted Auth/JWT checks
source_hash_rule: Postgres MD5(to_jsonb(pg_init_privs_row)::text), raw complete tuple stored

current_effective_safety_checks.observed: all 18 sensitive-relation checks deny SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE except pg_settings SELECT/UPDATE permitted to each role, a PostgreSQL system view subject to setting permission constraints
current_effective_safety_checks.observed_functions: anon/authenticated denied EXECUTE 6/6; service_role denied 4/6 system functions but can EXECUTE two provider Vault create/update secret functions; expected provider service-role privilege, not an exposure conclusion
current_effective_safety_checks.caveat: Catalog has_*_privilege checks are metadata only, not real hosted JWT authorization tests

semantic_findings: System PG catalogs commonly grant PUBLIC metadata reads via initial ACL; initial does not represent currently effective grants.
pg_subscription initial PUBLIC per-column SELECT exemptions must not be confused with effective table read; the latter tested DENIED.
pg_settings initial PUBLIC UPDATE is mediated by server-side GUC permissions and does not imply ALTER SYSTEM.
graphql/graphql_public initial schema usage by API roles does not prove active exposure.
Service role may call provider vault create/update secret; protect provider keys, but no confirmed member or anonymous access.
unverified: 63 intentionally withheld potentially sensitive GUC values
All 148 pg_rewrite rules not covered in this run
next_exact_cursor: pg_catalog.pg_rewrite ordinal 1/148 (sort by schema, relation, rule OID); then changed-definition drift and #96 provider coordination
